subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool design now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The feature is useful, but it changes core config, credentials, message delivery, session state, and Gateway trust boundaries in ways automation cannot approve safely.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and require peer identity, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer feature
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the `gateway.peers` direction and require this PR or a replacement to fix the blockers and provide live multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer to external bridges
options.body: If core federation is out of scope, document plugin/MCP bridge patterns and close implementation PRs only after the product decision is explicit.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical issue open and require peer identity, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history is strongest on the inspected gateway/session surfaces, with security and product input still needed from adjacent owners.
